correctness.rationale: Checked the actual equal-radius orthogonal intersection and Haar-width claim. At fixed y the section is a square, giving support r sqrt(u_y^2+(|u_x|+|u_z|)^2), hence W=2r sqrt(1+S), S=2|U_x U_z|. Independently, rotation by pi/4 gives S=|P-Q| where (P,Q,1-P-Q) has Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2) law. Its folded difference density is (1/pi) times the integral of [v(v+s)(1-s-2v)]^(-1/2) for 0<v<(1-s)/2. Substitution v=(1-s)sin^2(theta)/2 gives the displayed K with modulus sqrt((1-s)/(1+s)); the width Jacobian cancels sqrt(1+s). The elliptic endpoint expansion gives f_S(s)=log(8/s)/pi+O(s log(1/s)), and s=delta/r+delta^2/(4r^2) yields the stated full lower-tail constant and error. The density is smooth up to the other endpoint with limit 1/r; neither endpoint has atoms. Independent latitude/azimuth gives E S=(2/3)(2/pi). For 0<a<b<1, integrate the disk density over s^b<|x|<s^a and |z|<s/(2|x|): it is uniformly (1+o(1))/(2pi) there and the mass is (b-a)s log(1/s)/pi. Dividing by the full tail and exhausting interior intervals proves the conditional law and forces both |x| and |z| to zero in probability. Reflection gives the fair independent sign exactly for every positive threshold. Read the checker and notes without execution; the checker is a finite numerical diagnostic, not a proof of the limit.
